TO: The University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees FROM: Marc B.
Parlange, Ph.D., P.Eng.
President DATE: April 4, 2024 SUBJECT: Action Item: Approval to exercise the options to purchase 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island and execute all documents relating to these acquisitions.
Purpose of Submittal: The University is seeking approval from the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees to exercise the options to purchase and execute all documents necessary for the acquisition of the properties located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island and at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island.
Points to Consider: In April 1992, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the University of Rhode Island Foundation (the “Foundation”) with respect to land and buildings located at 75 and 85 Briar Lane, King ston, Rhode Island (the “Briar Lane Properties”) .

The Briar Lane Properties are currently the home of URI’s Police Department and its associated surface parking lot.
In May 2000, the University entered into a Lease/Purchase Agreement with the Foundation for land and buildings located at 177 Plains Road, Kingston, Rhode Island (the “Plains Road Property”).
The Plains Road Property currently houses URI’s Fire and Life Safety and Environment Health and Safety offices.
The agreements grant the University options (the “Options”) to purchase the Briar Lane Properties and the Plains Road Property (together, the “Properties”) for $1.00 each upon fulfilling the University’s lease payment obligations.
It has been determined by the University and confirmed by the Foundation that those obligations have been met.
Recommendation: After a thorough review by and with all of the appropriate stakeholders, I recommend that the University of Rhode Island Board of Trustees approve the request to authorize the exercise of the Options and direct that all required action be taken to consummate the acquisition of the Properties by the University.
Supporting Information: Please see attached Exercise Notices, Lease/Purchase Agreements from 1992 and 2000.

Proposed Motion of the Board: THAT, the Board of Trustees hereby approves the request to exercise the University’s options to acquire title to the properties located at 177 Plains Road and 75 and 85 Briar Lane, Kingston, Rhode Island, as granted to the University pursuant to the provisions of those Lease/Purchase Agreements related thereto and presented, and that the Board Chair, President and Vice President of Administration and Finance are each individually authorized, for and on behalf of the University and the Board of Trustees, to take all such actions and to execute all such documents as such person deems necessary and appropriate in furtherance of exercising such options and consummating the acquisition of the foregoing properties as recommended and presented.

Brief Fall 2020 Overview President Dooley shared that URI was purposeful in their decision-making process regarding Fall 2020 reopening.
The University conducted a thorough review of all possible reopening plans.
President Dooley stated that every decision was informed by CDC guidelines, the RI Department of Health, and on-campus health officials.
Deans, Faculty Senate, and Senior Leadership were heavily involved in these discussions and analyses as well.
Specifically, Qualitative Risk Analysis was used in this process.
Students’ and families’ opinions were heavily considered because the consensus was a strong desire to be back on campus rather than fully online.
This opinion was seen in national surveys across the country.
The University is currently planning to open the campus.

There will not be as many students living on campus as was traditionally seen in the past to reduce the risk of virus transmission.
URI pivoted and offered all summer sessions online, and it has been the highest summer enrollment ever recorded to date.
This summer, URI is investing in classroom technology to create the best teaching and learning environments for those classes offered remotely.
President Dooley shared that all of these plans are being discussed with an unknown budget.
The state is in a financial deficit, and it has impacted URI.
